name: Rehash merges two equality classes with a merge block

input.source_text: class Key { public property equal_id: Integer = 0 public property hash_code: Integer = 0 public fun ==(other: Object) -> Bool { @equal_id == other.equal_id() } public fun hash() -> Integer { @hash_code } public fun equal_id() -> Integer { @equal_id } } module M { public fun run() -> Array { mut k1 = Key.new(); k1.equal_id = 1; k1.hash_code = 10; mut k2 = Key.new(); k2.equal_id = 2; k2.hash_code = 10; mut k3 = Key.new(); k3.equal_id = 3; k3.hash_code = 20; mut k4 = Key.new(); k4.equal_id = 4; k4.hash_code = 20; mut h = %{}; h[k1] = 1; h[k2] = 2; h[k3] = 4; h[k4] = 8; k2.equal_id = 1; k4.equal_id = 3; mut calls = 0; h.rehash() { |kept, left, incoming, right| calls = calls + 1; (kept, left + right) }; [h.length(), calls, h.fetch(k1), h.fetch(k3)] } } M.run()

applicability.reason: Rehash merging is ordinary collection behaviour.
